title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Garden on 1973-04-02
lineage: SBD -> Rm (7.5 ips/2 Track) -> Dat -> Dat. Transfer Info: Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD (David Gans' Master Discs) -> EAC (Secure) -> SHN. CD -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a Boston Garden show where Here Comes Sunshine and a 16‑minute Eyes of the World blaze, backed by tight playing and stellar jams.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered SBD delivers an exceptionally clear mix that lets the band’s 1973 fire shine through. Highlights include a smoking Here Comes Sunshine, an epic Eyes of the World, and extended Playing in the Band, while the only real dip is the brief, over‑cooked “You Ain’t Woman Enough.” Overall the performance feels high‑energy and tightly locked.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both musical brilliance and recording fidelity; only a few minor criticisms appear, yielding a strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller remaster praised as crisp, well‑balanced and clean; occasional tiny file glitch noted but overall the board mix is clear with no significant drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set mixes standards with long jams (HCS, Miss Halfstep) and a few slower numbers; second set builds momentum with an expansive Playing in the Band, Weather Report Suite > Eyes, and a monster Eyes of the World that caps a high‑energy night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for scorching jams – especially on Greatest Story, Here Comes Sunshine and the 16‑minute Eyes of the World; his tone described as ‘excellent’ and ‘on fire.’
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a tight bass foundation and his spoken intro about “electric popcorn” before Playing in the Band; overall bass work called solid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s spacey, jazzy comping highlighted during Here Comes Sunshine and the Weather Report Suite, adding depth to the improvisations.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as driving and supportive throughout the long jams; no specific complaints.
